# `crates/tf_tree_ingest/testdata` — provenance

## `zstd_conformance.mcap` (1 069 bytes)

**Not a recording.** Nothing here came off a robot; there is no rosbag2 bag in this
repository. What this file *is* is the one piece of evidence that the pure-Rust zstd
decoder in `crate::decompress` agrees with **libzstd**, rather than merely with the
`ruzstd` encoder that writes every other compressed fixture.

That distinction is the whole reason the file is committed rather than generated at
test time: an encoder and a decoder from the same crate can agree with each other
and both disagree with the zstd that `rosbag2` and Foxglove actually link. Every
other compressed fixture in this crate proves round-trip. This one proves
conformance.

### What is ours and what is libzstd's

| Part | Produced by |
| --- | --- |
| MCAP file magic, `Header`, `Chunk`/`DataEnd`/`Footer` record framing | `tf_tree_ingest::fixture::chunked_mcap_bytes` (this repository) |
| `Schema`, `Channel`, `Message` record bodies; the CDR payloads | `tf_tree_ingest::fixture` + `tf_tree_ingest::cdr::encode_tf_message` |
| Each chunk's `uncompressed_size` and `uncompressed_crc` (CRC32 over the *uncompressed* records, per the MCAP specification) | this repository, computed before compression |
| **Each chunk's `records` field — the compressed bytes themselves** | **libzstd, via the `zstd` CLI** |

So the framing is ours and only the chunk payload is libzstd's. That is exactly the
split that makes it a conformance test of the decoder: our own CRC32 over our own
hash of the input is what checks libzstd's output.

### Exactly how it was generated

The generator reports the compressor's own version banner, so one command is the
whole transcript. Verbatim, with only the absolute path elided:

```text
$ cargo run -p tf_tree_ingest --features fixture --example gen_zstd_conformance
wrote …/crates/tf_tree_ingest/testdata/zstd_conformance.mcap (1069 B, 3 chunks, from 1982 uncompressed B) using *** Zstandard CLI (64-bit) v1.5.5, by Yann Collet ***
```

An earlier revision of this block showed a hand-written two-line output under the
same heading, which is not what the program prints. In a section whose whole job is
provenance, a transcript a reader cannot reproduce character for character costs
exactly the trust the section exists to earn.

**Regeneration is byte-reproducible on zstd 1.5.5**: re-running the command over the
committed file leaves it identical (`cmp` clean), which is verified rather than
assumed. So a diff on this file always means either the corpus or the compressor
changed, and never that the generator is nondeterministic.

The example pipes each chunk's records field through:

```text
zstd -19 --no-check -c -q
```

* `-19` rather than the default `-3`: the corpus is two kilobytes, so the cost is
  nothing, and a higher level exercises longer matches and larger Huffman tables —
  more of the format than a fast level would.
* `--no-check` omits zstd's own content checksum, **on purpose**. Nothing in
  `crate::decompress` verifies it (ruzstd computes a checksum and compares it to
  nothing), so leaving it in the frame would invite a reader to believe it is what
  validates the payload. The chunk CRC32 is the check that runs.

Regenerate it only when `fixture::conformance_recording` changes. The corpus is
frozen against this file: `tests/ingest.rs`'s `a_real_libzstd_recording_ingests`
compares the committed file's transforms against a control it writes from that
function, so a corpus change without a regeneration fails loudly rather than
quietly comparing two different recordings.

### Licence

Every byte is generated by code in this repository (MIT OR Apache-2.0) plus
`zstd`'s output over it. `zstd` is BSD-3-Clause / GPL-2.0 dual-licensed, and its
*output* carries no licence of its own — compressed data is not a derivative work
of the compressor. No third-party content is vendored here.

### The asymmetry, and how lz4 closes it differently

**There is no equivalent lz4 *file* here, because this host has no `lz4` CLI.** The
gap that would leave — `lz4_flex` encoding and `lz4_flex` decoding can agree with
each other and both disagree with the liblz4 rosbag2 and Foxglove link — is closed
from the other end instead, in
`decompress::tests::a_hand_authored_lz4_frame_decodes_per_the_specification`: an
82-byte LZ4 frame **written by hand from the frame and block formats**, which
`lz4_flex` has to agree with the specification about. Its sequences were chosen
rather than searched for, so one small frame carries a literal-length extension, a
match-length extension, a non-overlapping match and an overlapping one, plus the
frame's header checksum and its xxh32 content checksum.

Two things make it a conformance vector rather than a round-trip under another name,
and both are asserted rather than claimed: `lz4_flex`'s own encoder does **not**
produce those bytes for that input, and of the 656 single-bit perturbations of the
frame, 651 are caught — the five that are not are enumerated, with the format text
that makes each a don't-care.

It lives in source rather than beside this file because 82 bytes with a comment per
region is more use to a reader than an opaque blob, and because there is
deliberately no recipe that regenerates it: a vector regenerated by a tool is a
round-trip again.

**What is still missing is a whole lz4 *recording*** — the fixture above is one
frame, not an `.mcap` written by an independent implementation end to end. The
`lz4` CLI on the build host, or a fixture from the `mcap` CLI, would supply that;
whichever arrives first should land beside this file with its own row.
